headline: Grocery access and school funding rank first, environmental burden ranks worst here.
summary:
West Side neighborhoods North Lawndale, South Lawndale, Austin, and West Garfield Park make up Ward 24. It sits 47th citywide, with a score of 29.61, well down the list. Its strongest measures cluster around schools, food access, and neighborhood institutions. The ward ranks 1st in Chicago for mapped faith institutions, with 101 of them, and 1st for houses of worship per resident. It also ranks 1st for grocery stores and supermarkets per resident and 1st for per-pupil school spending, at $23,663 per student. Two modeled estimates land near the top as well, for daily leisure time and for how often residents are expected to spend an evening with neighbors.

The weaker numbers point to environmental and social strain. The ward ranks last in Chicago on the Chicago Environmental Justice Index, the city's measure of cumulative pollution and vulnerability where a higher score means a heavier burden, and last on the related share of residents living in an EJ-designated area. It also ranks last for modeled social trust, for the share of adults reporting frequent mental distress, for how connected people say they feel to their neighborhood, and for highly rated bars, of which the ward has zero. Together, the numbers describe a ward where schools and neighborhood institutions rank strong while the surrounding environment and public-health measures rank among the worst in the city.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers deserve a second look before they settle anything. The 1st-place rank for grocery stores per resident comes from a source that counts businesses by ZIP code, and ZIP codes were drawn for a different purpose than ward maps, so the two do not line up. Some of that count may really sit inside a neighboring ward instead. The last-place rank on the Environmental Justice Index runs into a version of the same problem, only with census tracts standing in for ZIP codes, and tracts don't follow ward lines any more neatly than ZIP codes do. Where a tract crosses the boundary, part of that score may end up credited to the ward next door. The last-place rank for social trust, 19 percent, comes from a statistical model built from citywide survey and demographic data. That estimate comes tagged low confidence, and it describes a pattern typical of wards built like this one on average, not something collected from Ward 24 residents directly.

news.headline: 'Missing Middle' Housing Program Breaks Ground On 27 Units In North Lawndale
news.note: The city broke ground on nine three-flats in North Lawndale as part of a 'Missing Middle' affordable housing program, with Ald. Monique Scott speaking at the event.

news.headline: Southside Blooms Expands Its Nationally Renowned Farm-To-Vase Operation To North Lawndale
news.note: A flower-farming nonprofit based in Englewood opened a second, larger location in North Lawndale for its retail and wholesale operations.

news.headline: Mixed-Use 'Lawndale ReDefined' Apartment Building Gets City Council Approval
news.note: The City Council approved zoning for a six-story, 59-unit mixed-income apartment building on a vacant lot in North Lawndale, with most units set aside as affordable.
